question: Does directly contrasting native conditional suffix likelihood under its original versus another length-matched observed context improve free Base coherence without losing Web quality?
observed_reason: Prior representation contrast improved retrieval but did not improve ordinary suffix likelihood or free generation. Natural correct versus cyclic contexts already showed measurable likelihood separation; reuse those diagnostics, do not rerun them
novelty: Native vocabulary-path likelihood, same exact suffix across contexts, same prefix token count, and observed natural source relations. Previous natural InfoNCE worked on separate last-valid hidden representations; previous outcome ranking used fixed synthetic opposite-label continuations and Web KL. This is not a coefficient, head, seed or parent rescue of either closed mechanism

literature.support: Sentence-level conditional likelihood supervision improved some cloze estimation results in an RNN; no Japanese10M free-generation claim. This context-swap logistic objective is an exploratory variant, not an exact reproduction
literature.title: Learning a Word-Level Language Model with Sentence-Level Noise Contrastive Estimation for Contextual Sentence Probability Estimation

literature.support: Conditional ranking-based noise estimation has a theoretical analysis under stated assumptions. Do not transfer consistency guarantees to this finite deterministic FIFO without proving its assumptions
